title: Mobile-first navigation
summary: Stacked links by default; one min-width media query turns them into a row on wider screens.
explanation: Mobile-first means the plain rules describe the phone layout, and media queries add to it as the screen grows. Here the header and its links stack vertically by default.
@media (min-width: 600px) applies only when the viewport is at least 600px wide. Inside it, the header becomes a row with the logo pushed to one side and the links to the other.
Writing it this way keeps the phone CSS small and simple, and wider layouts are additions rather than overrides.
tryThis: Switch the preview between 375 and 768: the layout changes at 600px.
Change 600px to 900px and try 768 again: it stays stacked.
Rewrite it desktop-first: put the row layout in the plain rules and use @media (max-width: 599px) for the stack.
